question: What is the primary purpose of a stock card in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To record the daily vital signs and health status of admitted patients
options.B: To document the financial salaries and allowances of hospital workers
options.C: To schedule the duty shifts and off-days of the ward nursing staff
options.D: To track the exact quantity and movement of a specific supply item

explanation: A stock card functions as a ledger specifically designed to monitor inventory levels, showing when items enter and leave the ward. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h1)

question: Why is inventory control considered a vital duty for ward nurses?

options.A: It prevents unexpected shortages of critical medical supplies during emergencies
options.B: It ensures that doctors write legible and accurate prescriptions daily
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for hospital management to buy new drugs
options.D: it stops patients from buying fake medications from outside pharmacies

explanation: Nurses manage ward stock so that life-saving items are always available when a patient suddenly deteriorates. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h1)

question: What does the balance column on a stock card represent?

options.A: The number of expired items thrown away that month
options.B: The maximum capacity the drug shelf can hold
options.C: The total amount of money spent on purchasing the item
options.D: The running total of remaining stock after each transaction

explanation: The balance updates continuously by adding receipts and subtracting issues to show what is currently available on the shelf. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h2)

question: Why must a nurse sign or initial every entry made on a stock card?

options.A: To calculate the monthly salary bonus due to the nursing unit
options.B: To prevent the pharmacy department from reducing future supplies
options.C: To prove that the nurse worked extra hours on that specific day
options.D: To ensure accountability and provide a clear trail for audits

explanation: Signatures establish personal responsibility for every movement of stock, which is essential for investigating discrepancies later. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h2)

question: What triggers a nurse to place a new order for a medical supply item?

options.A: When the hospital accountant visits the ward for an inspection
options.B: When the stock balance drops down to the reorder level
options.C: When the expiration date of the current batch is reached
options.D: When the storage shelf is completely empty and bare

explanation: The reorder level acts as an early warning system, giving enough time for new supplies to arrive before safety stock is touched. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h3)

question: A ward has a lead time of five days for syringes. What does this lead time actually mean?

options.A: It takes five days from placing the order until the syringes arrive on the ward
options.B: The ward will completely run out of all syringes in exactly five days
options.C: Syringes on the shelf will expire and spoil after five days of storage
options.D: Nurses must count the physical syringes every five days without fail

explanation: Lead time is the delivery window required for processing, packing, and transporting ordered goods to the requesting unit. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h3)

question: When is the best time for a nurse to record items taken from the stock cupboard?

options.A: Immediately after the items are removed for use
options.B: Whenever the physical shelf looks empty or disorganized
options.C: Only when the central store manager asks for a report
options.D: At the end of every working week on Friday afternoon

explanation: Immediate recording prevents forgotten transactions and keeps the running balance accurate throughout the shift. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h4)

question: What is the primary danger of delaying stock card updates until the end of the week?

options.A: Hospital management will reduce the overall budget of the nursing unit
options.B: The central store will automatically double the next order quantity
options.C: Arithmetic errors and forgotten items lead to inaccurate stock balances
options.D: The medications on the shelf will automatically change their expiry dates

explanation: Relying on memory hours or days later results in guessing quantities, which destroys the reliability of the inventory system. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h4)

question: How do seasonal disease trends influence how a nurse orders ward supplies?

options.A: They help nurses anticipate higher demand and order specific items ahead of time
options.B: They remove the need to calculate lead times when submitting requisitions
options.C: They dictate the exact time of day nurses must count the inventory
options.D: They change the physical maximum storage capacity of the drug cupboard

explanation: Anticipating disease patterns allows the ward to stock up on relevant treatments before an outbreak or seasonal surge hits. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h5)

question: A ward nurse notices that the stock of intravenous cannula size 18 has fallen below the reorder level. What immediate action should be taken?

options.A: Prepare and submit a requisition form to replenish the stock
options.B: Hide the remaining cannulas in a drawer so nobody else uses them
options.C: Wait until the very last cannula is used before telling anyone
options.D: Borrow supplies from another ward without recording the transaction

explanation: Hitting the reorder level is the signal to order more supplies immediately before a stockout occurs. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a necessary step when receiving new stock on the ward?

options.A: Verifying that the expiration dates on the products are acceptable
options.B: Checking the physical items against the quantities on the delivery note
options.C: Hiding the delivery notes so other staff members cannot read them
options.D: Inspecting the packaging for any signs of damage or leakage

explanation: Delivery notes are official records that should be kept accessible for audits, not hidden away. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h6)

question: Why is it important to check expiration dates immediately upon receiving new supplies?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial cost of each individual item
options.B: To determine how many nursing staff members are needed on duty
options.C: To decide which shelf in the storage cupboard looks the cleanest
options.D: To prevent accepting short-dated stock that might expire before use

explanation: Catching expired or near-expiry goods upon delivery allows the facility to return them before accepting responsibility for wasted items. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h6)
